name: alloc_shstk
prose: Precondition: called in process context with current->mm valid; size is the mapping length in bytes, addr is 0 or a requested fixed address, token_offset is only used when set_res_tok is true. Postcondition: takes mmap_write_lock(current->mm), calls do_mmap once for an anonymous private PROT_READ mapping (MAP_ABOVE4G, plus MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE when addr is nonzero, VM flags VM_SHADOW_STACK|VM_WRITE), and releases the lock. If set_res_tok is false or do_mmap returned an error value (IS_ERR_VALUE), it returns do_mmap's result unchanged. Otherwise it calls create_rstor_token(mapped_addr + token_offset, NULL): on success it returns the mapped address, with an 8-byte restore token (the passed address with bit 0 set) written at mapped_addr + token_offset - 8 (SS_FRAME_SIZE below the passed address); that helper fails if mapped_addr + token_offset is not 8-byte aligned or the user store faults, in which case the whole mapping of length size is removed with vm_munmap (its result ignored) and -EINVAL is returned as an unsigned long.
note: reviewer r15 right: token is stored at ssp-8 (shstk.c:50-69 create_rstor_token, SS_FRAME_SIZE=8 line 29), prose rewritten; r1 right (munmap on token failure now stated)

name: shstk_prctl
prose: Precondition: task is a valid task_struct, option is an ARCH_SHSTK_* request, arg2 is a user pointer for ARCH_SHSTK_STATUS and a feature bitmask otherwise. Postcondition, in order: for ARCH_SHSTK_STATUS it returns put_user(task->thread.features, arg2), i.e. 0 or -EFAULT; for ARCH_SHSTK_LOCK it ORs arg2 into task->thread.features_locked and returns 0; both of these apply whether or not task is current. If task != current, it clears the arg2 bits from task->thread.features_locked and returns 0 only for ARCH_SHSTK_UNLOCK when CONFIG_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE is enabled, and otherwise returns -EINVAL without changing state. For task == current: it returns -EPERM if arg2 overlaps features_locked, then -EINVAL if arg2 has more than one bit set; then for ARCH_SHSTK_DISABLE it returns wrss_control(false) if arg2 has ARCH_SHSTK_WRSS, shstk_disable() if it has ARCH_SHSTK_SHSTK, else -EINVAL; for any other option (ARCH_SHSTK_ENABLE, and also an UNLOCK or unknown option, which are not distinguished here) it returns shstk_setup() if arg2 has ARCH_SHSTK_SHSTK (which can allocate a shadow stack that the task then keeps), wrss_control(true) if it has ARCH_SHSTK_WRSS, else -EINVAL.
note: r15 right: shstk_setup() allocates a shadow stack that remains with the task (shstk.c:624-626), earlier 'no allocations retained' removed; r2 right on current-task UNLOCK falling through (shstk.c:619-625)

name: native_sched_clock
prose: Precondition: none; noinstr, takes no arguments, takes no lock. Postcondition: if the __use_tsc static branch is enabled it reads rdtsc() and returns __cycles_2_ns(tsc), which is the per-CPU cyc2ns offset plus mul_u64_u32_shr(tsc, mul, shift); the cyc2ns data is read through a seqcount-latch retry loop (__cyc2ns_read) and __cycles_2_ns itself does not disable or enable preemption (only cycles_2_ns, a different function, does). Otherwise it returns (jiffies_64 - INITIAL_JIFFIES) * (1000000000 / HZ), read with no locking. No state is modified.
note: r15 right: __cycles_2_ns (tsc.c:126-137) has no preempt_disable; cycles_2_ns (139-146) does. r2 'preemption must be disabled' is also wrong for this function: it never calls preempt_*

name: __load_segment_descriptor
prose: Precondition: ctxt is an initialized emulation context, selector/seg/cpl/transfer describe a segment load, desc is NULL or points to writable storage. Postcondition: returns X86EMUL_CONTINUE after calling ctxt->ops->set_segment(ctxt, selector, &seg_desc, base3, seg) and, if desc is non-NULL, copying the descriptor to *desc. In real mode (ctxt->mode == X86EMUL_MODE_REAL) it loads the existing descriptor via get_segment with base = selector << 4; in VM86 mode for seg <= GS it loads a synthesized present data descriptor (base selector<<4, limit 0xffff, type 3, dpl 3); neither does any descriptor-table read or check. Otherwise: a TR selector with the LDT bit set, a null selector (0-3) for CS or TR, or a null SS outside 64-bit mode or with RPL != cpl, returns X86EMUL_PROPAGATE_FAULT with #GP and error code 0; a null selector for other segments (and a null SS in 64-bit mode with RPL == cpl, using a synthesized descriptor) skips all further checks and loads. Non-null selectors: read_segment_descriptor errors are returned as is. After that, the error code is selector & 0xfffc and the vector is #TS for X86_TRANSFER_TASK_SWITCH, else #GP. A system descriptor loaded into a segment register (seg <= GS) returns X86EMUL_UNHANDLEABLE for X86_TRANSFER_CALL_JMP and #GP/#TS otherwise. SS, CS, TR, LDTR and DS/ES/FS/GS each have type/privilege checks that raise #GP/#TS on failure; CS additionally: transfer NONE raises the exception (with a WARN_ON_ONCE), RET to an outer privilege level (rpl > cpl) returns X86EMUL_UNHANDLEABLE, long-mode D/L conflict with EFER.LMA, and an invalid shadow-stack pointer (emulator_is_ssp_invalid, error code 0), and for CS the loaded selector becomes (selector & 0xfffc) | cpl in the protected-mode path only. A not-present descriptor raises #SS (for SS) or #NP with error code selector & 0xfffc. For a present non-system descriptor with the accessed bit clear, the bit is set via write_segment_descriptor (its error returned as is); for a system descriptor in 64-bit mode the upper base dword is read with linear_read_system (error returned as is) and a non-canonical base raises #GP with error code selector & 0xfffc. For TR the busy bit is set with ctxt->ops->cmpxchg_emulated, whose non-CONTINUE result is returned as is. Exceptions are recorded in ctxt->exception by emulate_exception, which returns X86EMUL_PROPAGATE_FAULT.
note: r15 right: CS rpl rewrite only in the protected-mode CS case (emulate.c:1652), real/VM86 branches goto load earlier; r2 right: TR-in-GDT check uses err_code 0 (err_code set to selector&0xfffc only at 1575, after the check at 1543); original: right, UNHANDLEABLE and passthrough errors added. Also corrected return constant to X86EMUL_PROPAGATE_FAULT (emulate.c:519), not PROPAGATE_EXCEPTION

name: ioapic_write_indirect
prose: Precondition: ioapic is a valid struct kvm_ioapic whose ioregsel names the register to write and val is the 32-bit value being written (callers serialize access with ioapic->lock; the function itself takes no lock). Postcondition: returns void. If ioregsel is IOAPIC_REG_VERSION or IOAPIC_REG_ARB_ID the write is ignored. If it is IOAPIC_REG_APIC_ID, ioapic->id becomes (val >> 24) & 0xf. Otherwise index = (ioregsel - 0x10) >> 1; if index >= IOAPIC_NUM_PINS the function returns with no change. Else the high half (ioregsel odd) or low half (ioregsel even) of redirtbl[index] is replaced by val, then remote_irr and delivery_status are restored to their old values; after that remote_irr is cleared if the entry is edge-triggered (so remote_irr survives only for level-triggered entries). If the mask bit differs from before, kvm_fire_mask_notifiers is called with the new mask. If the entry is level-triggered with the pin's irr bit set, unmasked and remote_irr clear, then if kvm_notify_irqfd_resampler succeeds the irr bit is cleared, otherwise ioapic_service(ioapic, index, false) is called and its return value is ignored. Finally, if delivery_mode is APIC_DM_FIXED, a scan-IOAPIC request is made for the vCPUs selected by the new dest_id/dest_mode, plus the vCPUs selected by the old dest_id (using the new dest_mode) if either dest_id or dest_mode changed; otherwise a scan-IOAPIC request is made for all vCPUs.
note: r15 right: old-destination lookup sets irq.dest_id = old_dest_id but irq.dest_mode from e->fields.dest_mode (new), ioapic.c:446-449; original reviewer right: remote_irr cleared for edge entries (385-386)

name: kvm_recalculate_apic_map
prose: Precondition: kvm is a valid struct kvm; the caller does not hold kvm->arch.apic_map_lock (the function takes it). Postcondition: returns void. If kvm->arch.apic_map_dirty reads CLEAN at entry it returns at once with no other effect. Otherwise it does WARN_ONCE if the VM has no in-kernel irqchip, takes apic_map_lock, and does cmpxchg DIRTY->UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS; if that cmpxchg observes CLEAN (someone else already updated) it unlocks and returns without touching apic_map, the APICv inhibits or the scan-IOAPIC request. Otherwise it clears xapic_id_mismatch, raises max_id to the largest x2APIC ID among present vCPUs, allocates a new map with kvzalloc and fills it per vCPU (physical and logical maps). If kvm_recalculate_phys_map returns -E2BIG the new map is freed and the whole build restarts from the cmpxchg (max_id is not reset, so it never decreases); any other error, or an allocation failure, leaves new as NULL. It then sets or clears APICV_INHIBIT_REASON_PHYSICAL_ID_ALIASED depending on new == NULL, LOGICAL_ID_ALIASED depending on new == NULL or logical_mode == KVM_APIC_MODE_MAP_DISABLED, and APIC_ID_MODIFIED depending on xapic_id_mismatch. It publishes new (possibly NULL, replacing the old map even on failure) with rcu_assign_pointer, does cmpxchg UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS->CLEAN (apic_map_dirty stays DIRTY if another updater set it DIRTY meanwhile), unlocks, frees the old map with kvfree_rcu if there was one, and calls kvm_make_scan_ioapic_request(kvm).
note: r15 wrong: kvfree_rcu(old) at lapic.c:511-512 and kvm_make_scan_ioapic_request at 514 are both in the code; r1/r2/original right and already covered (NULL map published at 485-502, dirty may stay DIRTY at 507-508)

name: pte_list_add
prose: Precondition: kvm->mmu_lock is held for write (kvm_rmap_lock asserts it), the caller does not already hold the rmap lock bit of rmap_head, and cache can supply a pte_list_desc when one is needed (a descriptor is allocated from cache only when the rmap currently holds exactly one spte, or when the head descriptor is full). Postcondition: takes the rmap lock, adds spte to the rmap headed by rmap_head, and releases the rmap lock with the updated value. If the rmap was empty, it stores the spte pointer directly. If it held one spte, a new descriptor from cache holds the old and new sptes (spte_count 2). If it was already a descriptor chain, spte is appended to the head descriptor, or to a new head descriptor taken from cache when the old head had PTE_LIST_EXT entries. Returns the number of sptes in the rmap before spte was added: 0 if it was empty, 1 if it held a single spte, otherwise the old head's tail_count + spte_count.
note: r15 right: allocation only for single-spte or full-head cases (mmu.c:1020-1021, 1036-1037); slice cut head

name: FNAME(page_fault)
prose: Precondition: vcpu and fault are valid; fault->is_tdp is expected to be false (checked with WARN_ON_ONCE only). Postcondition: walks the guest page table for fault->addr (with PFERR_RSVD masked out of the error code). If the walk fails it injects an emulated page fault into the guest unless fault->prefetch is set, and returns RET_PF_RETRY. Otherwise it fills fault->gfn, max_level and slot from the walk; if page_fault_handle_page_track says the gfn is write-tracked it calls shadow_page_table_clear_flood and returns RET_PF_WRITE_PROTECTED. It then returns mmu_topup_memory_caches's error if nonzero, then any non-RET_PF_CONTINUE result from kvm_mmu_faultin_pfn, all before taking mmu_lock. For non-EPT page tables, a supervisor write with CR0.WP clear on a non-writable guest PTE has the access bits adjusted (write allowed, user cleared, and exec cleared when SMEP is on). It then takes kvm->mmu_lock for write; if make_mmu_pages_available returns nonzero (-ENOSPC), or the fault is stale (RET_PF_RETRY), it jumps to out_unlock; otherwise the result is that of FNAME(fetch). On the out_unlock path it calls kvm_mmu_finish_page_fault(vcpu, fault, r) and releases mmu_lock, and returns r.
note: slice cut head (macro-generated FNAME(page_fault)); prose checked against paging_tmpl.h:765-847; dropped the overbroad 'no pfn reference leaked' claim; make_mmu_pages_available returns 0 or -ENOSPC (mmu.c:2835-2856)

name: sev_flush_asids
prose: Precondition: called with sev_bitmap_lock held, or at shutdown (comment at sev.c:111). Postcondition: finds the next set bit in sev_reclaim_asid_bitmap at or after min_asid; if that bit number is greater than max_asid it returns -EBUSY without taking sev_deactivate_lock or running WBINVD. Otherwise it takes sev_deactivate_lock for write, runs wbinvd_on_all_cpus(), issues the DF_FLUSH (sev_do_cmd(SEV_CMD_SNP_DF_FLUSH) if sev_snp_enabled, else sev_guest_df_flush), releases the lock, logs with pr_err if the command returned nonzero, and returns that command's return value (0 on success). It does not modify sev_reclaim_asid_bitmap and does not take or release sev_bitmap_lock.
note: r1 right (lock precondition now stated), r2/r15 about the formal contract moot: contract removed because the function reads a global bitmap and calls hardware

name: sev_es_sync_vmsa
prose: Precondition: vcpu->mutex is held (lockdep_assert_held); svm->sev_es.vmsa points to the VMSA save area to fill. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL without writing the VMSA if vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected is set, if svm->vcpu.guest_debug is nonzero, or if svm->vmcb->save.dr7 has any bit set outside DR7_FIXED_1. Otherwise it copies the whole VMCB save area into the VMSA, then overwrites rax, rbx, rcx, rdx, rsp, rbp, rsi, rdi (and r8-r15 when CONFIG_X86_64), rip from vcpu->arch.regs, xcr0, pkru, xss (from ia32_xss), dr6 from vcpu->arch, and sev_features from the VM's vmsa_features. Only if kvm->arch.vm_type != KVM_X86_DEFAULT_VM does it also copy the x87 state (dp, ftw, fsw, fcw, fop, rip, mxcsr, with ds/cs set to 0, and the 8 FP registers), the XMM area, and the YMM area (zero-filled when XFEATURE_YMM is absent) from the guest fpstate. It then emits the VMSA as a debug hex dump and returns 0.
note: r1 right (default VM skips FPU/AVX, sev.c:938-942); r2 right (dr7 & ~DR7_FIXED_1, sev.c:898); fixed text kept

name: svm_vcpu_run
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a valid SVM vCPU running on vcpu->cpu with interrupts and preemption such that the guest can be entered; run_flags may include KVM_RUN_FORCE_IMMEDIATE_EXIT and KVM_RUN_LOAD_GUEST_DR6. Postcondition: first copies RAX, RSP, RIP from vcpu->arch.regs into the VMCB save area; if NMI single-step is active and an event is being injected it disables NMI single-step and forces an immediate exit; if an immediate exit is forced it sends smp_send_reschedule(vcpu->cpu). If pre_svm_run(vcpu) returns nonzero, no guest entry is made: vcpu->run->exit_reason is set to KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY with fail_entry.hardware_entry_failure_reason = SVM_EXIT_ERR and fail_entry.cpu = vcpu->cpu, and EXIT_FASTPATH_EXIT_USERSPACE is returned (the register copy and other changes above are not undone). Otherwise it syncs the LAPIC to CR8, updates the VMCB ASID if it differs, copies CR2 into the VMCB, loads DR6 (guest value when KVM_RUN_LOAD_GUEST_DR6, else DR6_ACTIVE_LOW unless KVM_DEBUGREG_WONT_EXIT is set), then under CLGI/STGI swaps guest XSAVE state, DEBUGCTL (when LBR virtualization is off and it differs), and SPEC_CTRL (when X86_FEATURE_V_SPEC_CTRL is absent), and runs the guest via svm_vcpu_enter_exit. After the exit it copies CR2, RAX, RSP and RIP back into vcpu->arch only if the guest is not SEV-ES, clears regs_dirty, does the NMI kvm_before_interrupt/kvm_after_interrupt bookkeeping when the exit code is SVM_EXIT_NMI, syncs CR8 back, clears svm->next_rip, and in guest mode calls nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02, increments stat.nested_run when nested_run_pending was set and the exit code is not SVM_EXIT_ERR, and clears nested_run_pending. It then sets tlb_ctl to TLB_CONTROL_DO_NOTHING, marks the VMCB all clean, reads and resets the host async-PF flags on a #PF exit, clears the lazy-load bits in regs_avail, calls svm_handle_mce on a #MC exit, calls svm_complete_interrupts, caches nested.ctl.next_rip from the VMCB in guest mode, and returns svm_exit_handlers_fastpath(vcpu).
note: r15 right: CR2 copied back only when !sev_es_guest (svm.c:4382-4387); slice cut head (function starts at svm.c:4293)

name: BUILD_SVM_MSR_BITMAP_HELPERS(bool, test, test)
prose: Generated function svm_test_msr_bitmap_read(bitmap, msr), produced by the BUILD_SVM_MSR_BITMAP_HELPERS(bool, test, test) macro invocation at svm.h:678. Precondition: bitmap points to an MSR permission map covering at least the first three 2 KiB ranges (6144 bytes). The MSR is located by svm_msrpm_bit_nr: (msr & ~0x1fff) must be 0, 0xc0000000 or 0xc0010000 (ranges 0, 1, 2), giving bit number range*2048*8 + (msr & 0x1fff)*2; any other msr is out of range. Postcondition: if msr is out of range it returns true without reading the bitmap; otherwise it returns test_bit(bit_nr + 0, bitmap), true when the read-intercept bit is set. It modifies nothing.

name: handle_vmxon
prose: Precondition: the vCPU is handling a VMXON VM-exit with exit qualification and VMX instruction information available. Postcondition: in order, (1) CR4.VMXE clear: queues #UD, returns 1. (2) CPL != 0: injects #GP(0), returns 1. (3) already in VMX operation (vmx->nested.vmxon): returns nested_vmx_fail(VMXERR_VMXON_IN_VMX_ROOT_OPERATION), which is VMfailInvalid if there is no current VMCS (current_vmptr invalid and no valid enlightened VMCS) and VMfailValid with that error number otherwise, then skips the instruction. (4) host-state-invalid CR0 or CR4, or IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL lacking the lock or VMX-outside-SMX bits: injects #GP(0), returns 1. (5) nested_vmx_get_vmptr failure: if get_vmx_mem_address rejects the operand (it has queued an exception) it returns 1; if kvm_read_guest_virt fails it returns kvm_handle_memory_failure's result. (6) vmptr not a valid page address, or kvm_read_guest of the first 4 bytes fails, or those bytes differ from VMCS12_REVISION: VMfailInvalid. (7) otherwise stores vmptr in vmx->nested.vmxon_ptr and calls enter_vmx_operation; if it fails it returns its -ENOMEM (it frees whatever it had allocated: vmcs02, cached vmcs12, cached shadow vmcs12; the vmxon_ptr store is not reverted). (8) on success enter_vmx_operation has allocated vmcs02, cached vmcs12, cached shadow vmcs12, a shadow VMCS if enable_shadow_vmcs, set up the preemption timer, allocated vpid02, cleared last_vpid, set nested.vmxon, and updated PT interception in host-guest PT mode; the function returns nested_vmx_succeed(). The VMfail and VMsuccess results are the return value of kvm_skip_emulated_instruction, normally 1 but 0 if it asks for a userspace exit (for example single-stepping).
note: r15 right: get_vmx_mem_address failure returns 1 directly via nested_vmx_get_vmptr's *ret=1 (nested.c:5468-5473) and VMXON-in-root yields VMfailInvalid or VMfailValid via nested_vmx_fail (192-205); r2 right: revision read uses kvm_read_guest -> VMfailInvalid (5648-5650); original right: -ENOMEM (5565)

name: vmx_set_nested_state
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a valid vCPU, kvm_state is the kernel copy of a user-supplied struct kvm_nested_state, and user_kvm_nested_state is the user buffer holding the vmx data (vmcs12, shadow vmcs12). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, before changing any nested state, if the format is not KVM_STATE_NESTED_FORMAT_VMX; if vmxon_pa is INVALID_GPA and (smm flags are set, vmcs12_pa is not INVALID_GPA, or flags other than KVM_STATE_NESTED_EVMCS are set); if vmxon_pa is valid but the guest lacks X86_FEATURE_VMX or vmxon_pa is not a valid page address; or if SMM/hdr flags are inconsistent (both SMM guest-mode and GUEST_MODE; unknown smm or hdr flags; flags that are not allowed for the current is_smm(); SMM_GUEST_MODE without SMM_VMXON; EVMCS flag without VMX capability or enabled eVMCS). It then calls vmx_leave_nested, tearing down any existing nested state. If vmxon_pa is INVALID_GPA it returns 0. Otherwise it stores vmxon_ptr and calls enter_vmx_operation (returning its error, -ENOMEM, if it fails). If kvm_state->size is smaller than a header plus vmcs12 it returns -EINVAL when GUEST_MODE, EVMCS, or a vmcs12_pa is given and 0 otherwise. It then sets the current vmptr from vmcs12_pa (-EINVAL if it equals vmxon_pa or is not a valid page address), or, with CONFIG_KVM_HYPERV and the EVMCS flag, marks the eVMCS pointer map-pending and requests KVM_REQ_GET_NESTED_STATE_PAGES, or else returns -EINVAL. It applies the SMM vmxon/guest_mode flags, copies vmcs12 from user memory (-EFAULT on failure), returns -EINVAL on a revision-id mismatch, and returns 0 if the GUEST_MODE flag is not set. With GUEST_MODE it sets nested_run_pending and mtf_pending from the flags; if vmcs12 enables shadow VMCS with a valid link pointer it requires room in size (else -EINVAL), copies the shadow vmcs12 (-EFAULT on failure) and checks its revision and shadow bit (else -EINVAL); it records the preemption timer deadline if flagged; runs nested_vmx_check_controls, check_host_state and check_guest_state (any failure gives -EINVAL); then calls nested_vmx_enter_non_root_mode and returns its status if nonzero (an enum value, NVMX_VMENTRY_VMFAIL/VMEXIT/KVM_INTERNAL_ERROR, not a negative errno). From the shadow-vmcs12 size check onward, failures clear nested_run_pending and return; earlier failures after vmx_leave_nested leave the new, partially established VMXON/current-vmptr state in place. On success it requests KVM_REQ_EVENT if mtf_pending is set and returns 0.
note: slice cut head and function name outside slice (function is vmx_set_nested_state at nested.c:6976); returned error is an nvmx_vmentry_status enum (nested.h:14-17), not always a negative errno

name: tdx_handle_exit
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a TDX vCPU whose tdx->vp_enter_ret and exit reason were set by the last TD entry; fastpath is the fastpath result. Postcondition, in order: returns 1 if fastpath != EXIT_FASTPATH_NONE. Returns -EIO (after KVM_BUG_ON(1)) if vp_enter_ret equals EXIT_REASON_EPT_MISCONFIG exactly. If vp_enter_ret has the TDX_SW_ERROR pattern it does KVM_BUG_ON(!kvm_rebooting) and goes to the unhandled-exit path. If tdx_failed_vmentry(vcpu) it sets run->exit_reason = KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY, fail_entry.hardware_entry_failure_reason = exit_reason.full, fail_entry.cpu = vcpu->arch.last_vmentry_cpu, and returns 0. If TDX_ERROR or TDX_NON_RECOVERABLE is set and the basic exit reason is not a triple fault, it logs and goes to the unhandled-exit path. Otherwise it dispatches on the basic exit reason: triple fault sets KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN, clears mmio_needed and returns 0; EXTERNAL_INTERRUPT increments stat.irq_exits and returns 1; OTHER_SMI returns 1; EXCEPTION_NMI, CPUID, HLT (kvm_emulate_halt_noskip), TDCALL, VMCALL, IO_INSTRUCTION, MSR_READ, MSR_WRITE (after loading rcx/rax/rdx from the saved TDVMCALL args), EPT_MISCONFIG and EPT_VIOLATION return the value of their handler. Any other reason, and the TDX software error and unrecoverable paths above, set KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR with suberror KVM_INTERNAL_ERROR_UNEXPECTED_EXIT_REASON, ndata 2, data[0] = vp_enter_ret, data[1] = last_vmentry_cpu, and return 0.
note: unreviewed; rewritten with the real check order (tdx.c:2039-2148); handler return values are not limited to 0/1 in the source (e.g. negative errors from handlers)

name: tdx_has_emulated_msr
prose: Precondition: none; index is any 32-bit MSR number. Postcondition: returns true if index is one of MSR_IA32_UCODE_REV (0x8b), MSR_IA32_ARCH_CAPABILITIES, MSR_IA32_POWER_CTL, MSR_IA32_CR_PAT, MSR_MTRRcap, 0x200-0x26f (MTRRphysBase_MSR(0) through MSR_MTRRfix4K_F8000), MSR_MTRRdefType, MSR_IA32_TSC_DEADLINE, MSR_IA32_MISC_ENABLE, MSR_PLATFORM_INFO, MSR_MISC_FEATURES_ENABLES, MSR_IA32_APICBASE, MSR_EFER, MSR_IA32_FEAT_CTL, MSR_IA32_MCG_CAP, MSR_IA32_MCG_STATUS, MSR_IA32_MCG_CTL, MSR_IA32_MCG_EXT_CTL, 0x400-0x47f (MCx_CTL for KVM_MAX_MCE_BANKS = 32 banks), 0x280-0x29f (MCx_CTL2), or MSR_KVM_POLL_CONTROL (0x4b564d05). For indices 0x800-0x8ff (x2APIC) it returns true except for 0x808, 0x80a, 0x80b, 0x810, 0x818 and 0x820; the source writes the ISR, TMR and IRR cases as X2APIC_MSR(APIC_ISR) ... X2APIC_MSR(APIC_ISR + APIC_ISR_NR) and the end of each range maps to the same MSR as its start, so only the first MSR of each ISR/TMR/IRR block is excluded. For every other index it returns false. It reads no state.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (result == 1) <==> ((index == 0x8b) || (index == 0x10a) || (index == 0x1fc) || (index == 0x277) || (index == 0xfe) || ((0x200 <= index) && (index <= 0x26f)) || (index == 0x2ff) || (index == 0x6e0) || (index == 0x1a0) || (index == 0xce) || (index == 0x140) || (index == 0x1b) || (index == 0xc0000080) || (index == 0x3a) || (index == 0x179) || (index == 0x17a) || (index == 0x17b) || (index == 0x4d0) || ((0x400 <= index) && (index <= 0x47f)) || ((0x280 <= index) && (index <= 0x29f)) || (index == 0x4b564d05) || (((0x800 <= index) && (index <= 0x8ff)) && !((index == 0x808) || (index == 0x80a) || (index == 0x80b) || (index == 0x810) || (index == 0x818) || (index == 0x820)))); */
note: unreviewed; prior text/contract were wrong: ISR/TMR/IRR excluded ranges collapse to single MSRs (tdx.c:2204-2206, X2APIC_MSR(r)=0x800+(r>>4), APIC_ISR_NR=0x8), and MSR_KVM_POLL_CONTROL is 0x4b564d05, not 0x4b (kvm_para.h:57)

name: tdx_get_msr
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a TDX vCPU and msr->index is set; msr->host_initiated is meaningful. Postcondition: for MSR_IA32_FEAT_CTL it sets msr->data to FEAT_CTL_LOCKED, plus FEAT_CTL_LMCE_ENABLED when vcpu->arch.mcg_cap has MCG_LMCE_P, and returns 0. For MSR_IA32_MCG_EXT_CTL it returns 1 when the access is not host-initiated and MCG_LMCE_P is not set; otherwise it sets msr->data to vcpu->arch.mcg_ext_ctl and returns 0. For any other index it returns 1 if tdx_has_emulated_msr(index) is false, else returns kvm_get_msr_common(vcpu, msr).
note: unreviewed; checked tdx.c:2222-2245

name: tdx_set_msr
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a TDX vCPU and msr->index, msr->data and msr->host_initiated are set. Postcondition: for MSR_IA32_MCG_EXT_CTL it returns 1 if the access is not host-initiated and MCG_LMCE_P is not set in vcpu->arch.mcg_cap, or if msr->data has bits outside MCG_EXT_CTL_LMCE_EN; otherwise it stores msr->data in vcpu->arch.mcg_ext_ctl and returns 0. For any other index it returns 1 if the index is MSR_IA32_APICBASE, MSR_EFER or MSR_IA32_FEAT_CTL, or if tdx_has_emulated_msr(index) is false; otherwise it returns kvm_set_msr_common(vcpu, msr).
note: unreviewed; checked tdx.c:2247-2265

name: handle_dr
prose: Precondition: vcpu is a VMX vCPU handling a MOV-DR VM-exit; the debug register number and the general register come from the exit qualification. Postcondition: returns 1 (with #UD queued by kvm_require_dr) if the debug register number is 4 or 5 and CR4.DE is set. If CPL > 0 it goes to the common exit with err = 1. If guest DR7 has DR7_GD: when KVM_GUESTDBG_USE_HW_BP is set it fills vcpu->run->debug.arch (dr6 = DR6_BD | DR6_ACTIVE_LOW, dr7, pc, exception = DB_VECTOR), sets exit_reason to KVM_EXIT_DEBUG and returns 0; otherwise it queues #DB with DR6_BD and returns 1. Else if vcpu->guest_debug is 0 it clears CPU_BASED_MOV_DR_EXITING, sets KVM_DEBUGREG_WONT_EXIT in switch_db_regs and returns 1 without skipping the instruction. Otherwise it performs the access: for a MOV from DR it writes kvm_get_dr to the register (err 0); for a MOV to DR it calls kvm_set_dr (err is its result). It then returns kvm_complete_insn_gp(vcpu, err): if err is nonzero it injects #GP(0) and returns 1; if err is 0 it returns kvm_skip_emulated_instruction's value, which is 1 normally and 0 if the skip fails or single-step requests a userspace exit.
note: r15 right: kvm_complete_insn_gp returns 0, not 1, when the instruction cannot be skipped (x86.c:941-949, 8851-8873); original/r2 right: success path returns the skip result, 0 is not only the userspace-debug exit

name: vmx_init
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns -EOPNOTSUPP if kvm_is_vmx_supported() is false. Otherwise it calls hv_init_evmcs(), then returns -EIO if setup_vmcs_config() returns a negative value. It then calls kvm_x86_vendor_init(&vt_init_ops) and returns its error code if nonzero. Next it calls vmx_setup_l1d_flush(vmentry_l1d_flush_param); if that fails it calls kvm_x86_vendor_exit() and returns its error code (this is the only path that calls kvm_x86_vendor_exit). On success it initializes the per-CPU loaded_vmcss_on_cpu list head and calls pi_init_cpu() for every possible CPU, runs vmx_check_vmcs12_offsets(), and returns 0. vmx_init itself takes no lock.
note: r1/r2/r15 reviewers' complaints are about the old formal contract; contract removed (touches globals). Checked vmx.c:8698-8748; slice shows only the tail of the file region
